Horizontal position of content when viewport is wider than content width. 0.0 is far left, 0.5 is center, 1.0 is far right.
Vertical position of content when viewport is taller than content height. 0.0 is top, 0.5 is center, 1.0 is bottom.
Forces a certain orientation of the screen from the operating system.
Hardware context scaling (if available).
Improves performance at the cost of latency and more video stuttering. Use only if full speed cannot be obtained otherwise.
Synchronize the output video of the graphics card to the refresh rate of the screen. Recommended.

Use a custom swap interval for VSync. Effectively reduces monitor refresh rate by the specified factor. 'Auto' sets factor based on core-reported frame rate, providing improved frame pacing when running e.g. 30 fps content on a 60 Hz display or 60 fps content on a 120 Hz display.

VSync is enabled until performance falls below the target refresh rate. Can minimize stuttering when performance falls below real time, and be more energy efficient. Not compatible with 'Frame Delay'.
Hard-synchronize the CPU and GPU. Reduces latency at the cost of performance.
Set how many frames the CPU can run ahead of the GPU when using 'Hard GPU Sync'.
Tells the video driver to explicitly use a specified buffering mode.

WARNING: Rapid flickering may cause image persistence on some displays. Use at your own risk // Insert black frame(s) between frames. Can greatly reduce motion blur by emulating CRT scan out, but at cost of brightness.

Adjust number of black frames in total BFI scan out sequence. More equals higher motion clarity, less equals higher brightness. Not applicable at 120hz as there is only 1 BFI frame to work with total. Settings higher than possible will limit you to the maximum possible for your chosen refresh rate.

WARNING: Rapid flickering may cause image persistence on some displays. Use at your own risk // Simulates a basic rolling scanline over multiple sub-frames by dividing the screen up vertically and rendering each part of the screen according to how many sub-frames there are.

WARNING: Rapid flickering may cause image persistence on some displays. Use at your own risk // Simulates a basic rolling scanline over multiple sub-frames by dividing the screen up vertically and rendering each part of the screen according to how many sub-frames there are.
Vertical refresh rate of your screen. Used to calculate a suitable audio input rate. This will be ignored if 'Threaded Video' is enabled.

Run additional core logic to reduce latency. Single Instance runs to a future frame, then reloads the current state. Second Instance keeps a video-only core instance at a future frame to avoid audio state issues. Preemptive Frames runs past frames with new input when needed, for efficiency.
The number of frames to run ahead. Causes gameplay issues such as jitter if the number of lag frames internal to the game is exceeded.
Reduces latency at the cost of a higher risk of video stuttering.
Adjust effective 'Frame Delay' dynamically.
Influences how input polling is done in RetroArch. Setting it to 'Early' or 'Late' can result in less latency, depending on your configuration.
Hide the warning message that appears when using Run-Ahead and the core does not support save states.
The number of milliseconds to wait to get a complete input sample. Use it if you have issues with simultaneous button presses (Android only).

retroarch.l: Sync to Exact Content Framerate (G-Sync, FreeSync)
retroarch.desc: No deviation from core requested timing. Use for Variable Refresh Rate screens (G-Sync, FreeSync, HDMI 2.1 VRR).
The maximum rate at which content will be run when using fast-forward (e.g., 5.0x for 60 fps content = 300 fps cap). If set to 0.0x, fast-forward ratio is unlimited (no FPS cap).
Skip frames according to fast-forward rate. This conserves power and allows the use of third party frame limiting.
The rate that content will play when using slow-motion.
Return to a previous point in recent gameplay. This causes a severe performance hit when playing.
The number of frames to rewind per step. Higher values increase the rewind speed.
The amount of memory (in MB) to reserve for the rewind buffer. Increasing this will increase the amount of rewind history.
Each time the rewind buffer size value is increased or decreased, it will change by this amount.
Audio volume (in dB). 0 dB is normal volume, and no gain is applied.
Mute audio.
Synchronize audio. Recommended.
Automatically mute audio when using fast-forward.
Speed up audio when fast-forwarding. Prevents crackling but shifts pitch.
Automatically mute audio when using rewind.
Enable audio output.
Maximum audio latency in milliseconds. The driver aims to keep actual latency at 50% of this value. Might not be honored if the audio driver can't provide given latency.
Helps smooth out imperfections in timing when synchronizing audio and video. Be aware that if disabled, proper synchronization is nearly impossible to obtain.
The maximum change in audio input rate. Increasing this enables very large changes in timing at the cost of an inaccurate audio pitch (e.g. running PAL cores on NTSC displays).
Lower this value to favor performance/lower latency over audio quality, increase for better audio quality at the expense of performance/lower latency.
Audio output sample rate.
Automatically make a save state when content is closed. This save state is loaded on startup if 'Auto Load State' is enabled.
Automatically load the auto save state on startup.
Automatically save the non-volatile SaveRAM at a regular interval (in seconds).

retroarch.l: Don't Overwrite SaveRAM on Loading Save State
retroarch.desc: Block SaveRAM from being overwritten when loading save states. Might potentially lead to buggy games.
Before making a save state, the save state index is automatically increased. When loading content, the index will be set to the highest existing index.

retroarch.l: Maximum Auto-Increment Save States to Keep
retroarch.desc: Limit the number of save states that will be created when 'Increment Save State Index Automatically' is enabled. If limit is exceeded when saving a new state, the existing state with the lowest index will be deleted. A value of '0' means unlimited states will be recorded.
Ignore analog stick movements below deadzone value.
Adjust the sensitivity of analog sticks.

rpcs3.desc: Affects maximum amount of PPU threads running concurrently, the value of 1 has very low compatibility with games.
Creates PPU logs.
Limits the maximum number of threads used for the initial PPU and SPU module compilation.
Searches the game's directory and precompiles extra PPU and SPU modules during boot.
Sets special MXCSR flags to debug errors in SSE operations.
Enable SPU RdEventStat spin.
Disable SPU GETLLAR spin optimization.
Creates SPU logs.
Creates MFC logs.
Some SPU stages are sensitive to race conditions and allowing a limited number at a time helps alleviate performance stalls.
Try to detect loop conditions in SPU kernels and use them as scheduling hints.
Limits the maximum number of SPURS threads in each thread group.
This option controls the SPU analyser, particularly the size of compiled units.
Accurately processes SPU DMA operations.
Accurately emulates SPU reservations.
Accurately processes PPU DCBZ instruction.
Forces RSX pauses on SPU MFC_GETLLAR and SPU MFC_PUTLLUC operations.
Give PPUs an execution advantage when the SPUs are using reservations.
"Fast" is the least accurate setting, RSX does not emulate atomic FIFO buffer.
When enabled, SPU performance is measured at runtime.
Control accuracy to SPU float vectors processing.

rpcs3.k: Accurate PPU 128-byte Reservation Op Max Length
rpcs3.desc: When enabled, PPU atomic operations will operate on entire cache line data, as opposed to a single 64bit block of memory when disabled.
Accurately set Saturation Bit values in PPU backends.
Respect Non-Java Mode Bit values for vector ops in PPU backends.
Accurately set NaN results in vector instructions in PPU backends.
Accurately set FPCC Bits in PPU backends.
Increases the amount of usable system memory to match a DECR console and more.
Allows to hook some functions like 'memcpy' replacing them with high-level implementations.
Changes the sleep period accuracy.
Measure certain events and print a chart after the emulator is stopped.
Vulkan is the fastest renderer.
This setting will be ignored if the Resolution Scale is set to anything other than 100%!
Leave this on 16:9 unless you have a 4:3 monitor.
Off is the fastest option.
Emulate PS3 multisampling layout.
Controls the precision level of generated shaders.
Enables vertical synchronization to eliminate tearing.
Enable this option if you get missing graphics or broken lighting ingame.
Writes depth buffer values to vm memory.
Initializes render target memory using vm memory.
Initializes render target memory using vm memory.
Obey RSX memory tiling configuration when writing GPU data to vm memory.
Dump game shaders to file.
Enables the selected API's inbuilt debugging functionality.
Provides a graphical overlay of various debugging information.
Enables use of classic OpenGL buffers which allows capturing tools to work with RPCS3 e.g RenderDoc.
Force all texture transfer, scaling and conversion operations on the GPU.
Overrides the aspect ratio and stretches the image to the full display area.
Only useful when debugging differences in GPU hardware.
Enforces strict compliance to the API specification.
Controls how RPCS3 resolves render targets where color and depth alias the same memory.
Disables running occlusion queries.
Disables all video output and PS3 graphical rendering.
Disables the vertex cache.
Disables RSX FIFO optimizations completely.
Emulate depth comparison operations where desktop hardware behavior differs from PS3, usually EQUAL comparison modes.
Forces emulation of all blit and image manipulation operations on the CPU.
Disables the loading and saving of shaders from and to the shader cache in the data directory.
Disables the custom Vulkan memory allocator and reverts to direct calls to VkAllocateMemory/VkFreeMemory.
Forces texture flushing even in situations where it is not necessary/correct.
Offloads some RSX operations to a secondary thread.
Forces MSAA to use the host GPU's resolve capabilities for all sampling operations.
Sets the 3D stereo rendering mode (only available in custom configurations with a default resolution of 720p).
Higher values increase sharpness of textures on sloped surfaces at the cost of GPU resources.
Number of threads to use for the shader compiler backend.
Allows the host GPU to synchronize with CELL directly.
Disables Fast Math for MSL shaders, which may violate the IEEE 754 standard.
Force host memory management calls to be inlined instead of handled asynchronously.
Final image filtering.
Enables recording with overlays.
Disables use of hardware-native color-space remapping formats such as _sRGB and _SNORM suffixes.
Force use of programmable blending for backends that support the feature.
Disable upscaling on the RSX image scaling and rotation engine (NV3089) outputs.
Stream textures to GPU in parallel with 3D rendering using asynchronous compute.
Determines how to schedule GPU async compute jobs when using asynchronous streaming.

rpcs3.l: Use Re-BAR memory for GPU uploads
rpcs3.desc: When enabled, Vulkan will try to use PCI-e resizable bar address space for GPU uploads of timing-sensitive data.
Enables or disables the performance overlay.
Enables or disables the framerate graph.
Enables or disables the frametime graph.
Controls the amount of information displayed on the performance overlay.
Sets the on-screen position (quadrant) of the performance overlay.
Sets the horizontal distance to the screen border relative to the screen quadrant (measured in %).
Sets the vertical distance to the screen border relative to the screen quadrant (measured in %).
Centers the performance overlay horizontally and overrides the horizontal margin.
Centers the performance overlay vertically and overrides the vertical margin.
Position overlay relative to the full window surface, enabling placement outside game's render area.
Cubeb uses a cross-platform approach and supports audio buffering, so it is the recommended option.
Controls which PS3 audio API is used.
Controls which avport is used to sample audio data from.
Saves all audio as a raw wave file.
Uses 16-bit audio samples instead of default 32-bit floating point.
Determines the sound format of the emulation.
Determines the sound format of RPCS3.
Enables audio buffering, which reduces crackle/stutter but increases audio latency.
Enables time stretching - requires buffering to be enabled.
When this mode is on, savestates are loaded and paused on the first frame.
When this mode is on, emulation exits when saving and the savestate file is concealed after its load, preventing reuse by RPCS3.
When this mode is on, SPU emulation prioritizes savestate compatibility, however, it may reduce performance slightly.
Enables use of native HUD within the game window that can interact with game controllers.
When enabled, opening the home menu will also pause emulation.
Play music during boot sequence if available.

supermodel.desc: PowerPC frequency (default varies by stepping) 0 = the game's own (varies by board stepping).
Run emulation on several threads (off: everything in one thread).
Run graphics rendering in separate thread [Default]
Use 8 texture maps for decoding (legacy engine)
Emulate the sound board (sound effects).
Relative front/rear balance in % [Default: 0]
Number of sound channels to use on host [Default: 4]
Usual values: 57.52416, 60.
Emulate the Digital Sound Board (MPEG music).
Volume of SCSP-generated sound in %, applies only when Digital Sound Board is present [Default: 100]
Digital Sound Board volume in % [Default: 100]
Legacy SCSP engine by ElSemi
Enable force feedback (DirectInput, XInput)
New 3D engine by Ian Curtis [Default]
Enable proper quad rendering
Resolution [Default: 496,384]
Resolution [Default: 496,384]
Supersampling (range 1-8)
CRT color emulation (range 0-5)
2D layer upscaling filter mode (range 0-3)
Expand 3D field of view to screen width
Fit viewport to resolution, ignoring aspect ratio
When wide-screen mode is enabled, also expand the 2D background layer to screen width
Lock to vertical refresh rate [Default]
Lock the frame rate (off: run as fast as possible).
Refresh rate in Hz; the real Model 3 runs at 57.524. Usual values: 57.5, 60.
Display frame rate in window title bar
Crosshairs configuration for gun games: 0=none [Default], 1=P1 only, 2=P2 only, 3=P1 & P2
Crosshair style: vector or bmp. [Default: vector]
Disables white flash when games disable 3D rendering
Swap left and right audio channels
Enable net board
Simulate the net board [Default]
Write memory regions to files on exit
Write textures to bitmap image files on exit

vita3k.desc: Automatically select modules to load. Recommended for most apps.
Enable Dynarmic JIT optimizations. Improves performance.
Select the preferred backend renderer. Vulkan is recommended for most systems.
Set the renderer accuracy level for Vulkan. High accuracy may improve visuals but reduce performance.
Scale the games resolution by a multiplier.
Speed hack, disabling turns off surface syncing between CPU and GPU. Surface syncing is needed by a few games.
Select the final image filter to apply.
Memory mapping improved performance, reduces memory usage and fixes many graphical issues. However, it may be unstable on some GPUs.
Enable V-Sync for OpenGL. Reduces screen tearing.
Technique to increase the sharpness of textures which are sloped relative to the viewer.
Allow pipelines to be compiled concurrently on multiple concurrent threads.
Import replacement textures from the textures folder.
Export textures used by the app to the textures folder.
Format to export textures in.
Game hack. May double the framerate from 30 FPS to 60 FPS in some games, but can cause some games to run twice as fast.
Enable shader caching. Reduces stuttering on subsequent runs.
Pass generated Spir-V shader directly to driver.
Enable the texture cache. Improves performance in games at the cost of additional VRAM usage.
Select the audio backend. Cubeb is recommended for most systems.
Set the in-game audio volume.
Enable advanced audio library NGS support.
Enable PlayStation TV mode.
Select which button acts as the Enter/Confirm button. Some apps ignore this setting.
Set the system language reported to applications.
Set the date format used by the emulated system.
Set the time format used by the emulated system.
Add an artificial delay to file loading. This is required for some games that load files too quickly compared to real hardware (e.g., Silent Hill).
Stretch the display area to fill the entire window, ignoring the original aspect ratio.
Check the box to get a pixel perfect rendering with HD resolutions (1080p, 4K) in fullscreen on a 16:9 aspect ratio monitor at the price of slight cropping at the top and the bottom of the screen.
Log active shader programs.
Log shader uniform values.
Save color surfaces to files.
Enable Vulkan validation layers. Useful for debugging but reduces performance.
Pretend to be signed in to PlayStation Network (but offline).

xenia.desc: Allows loading of plugins/trainers from plugins\title_id\plugin.xex. Plugin are homebrew xex modules which can be used for making mods. This feature is experimental.
Enables custom patching functionality
Executable to launch from the .iso or the package instead of default.xex or the module specified by the game. Leave blank to launch the default module.
Scalar used to speed or slow time (1x, 2x, 1/2x, etc).
Generate no code for powerpc trap instructions, can result in better performance in games that aggressively check with trap.

xenia.l: D3D12 allow variable refresh rate and tearing
xenia.desc: In fullscreen, allow using variable refresh rate on displays supporting it. On displays not supporting VRR, screen tearing may occur in certain cases.
Use bindless resources where available - may improve performance, but may make debugging more complicated.
Forces anisotropic filtering (AF) for eligible textures.

Compile shaders and create pipelines asynchronously in background threads. Eliminates shader compilation stutter but may cause brief rendering artifacts while pipelines are being created. When disabled, pipelines are created synchronously which causes stutter but no visual artifacts.
Refresh state of memory pages to enable gpu written data. (Use for 'Team Ninja' Games to fix missing character models)

Route decal host render target draws with polygon offset through shader depth. This avoids Z-fighting in games that rely on tiny depth bias values that host fixed function depth bias cannot reproduce reliably.This likely causes some minor performance penalty, but the cost should be minimal if only a small portion of the scene is affected.
Surface pitch in pixels at or below render targets skip being upscaled by draw_resolution_scale_x/y. 0 disables it.
Integer pixel width scale used for scaling the rendering resolution opaquely to the game.
Integer pixel width scale used for scaling the rendering resolution opaquely to the game.
Apply offsets from texture fetch instructions taking resolution scale into account for render-to-texture, for more correct shadow filtering, bloom, etc., in some cases.
Use host depth clamping instead of near and far plane clipping when guest clipping is enabled. X/Y/W clipping is unaffected. On Vulkan, this requires depthClamp support.
Maximum frames per second. 0 = Unlimited frames.
Handle shaders that sample 3D textures as 2D by creating a 2D texture from slice 0 of the guest memory.

Allow texture and vertex fetch constants with invalid type - generally unsafe because the constant may contain completely invalid values, but may be used to bypass fetch constant type errors in certain games until the real reason why they're invalid is found.
Allows games to read data from pages that are marked as no access.

Round mulsc products toward zero instead of to nearest even. This fixes bad geometry in several Volition Engine titles and possibly others. This rounding behavior hasn't been confirmed on real hardware, so it's disabled by default.
Controls hardware occlusion query behavior for EVENT_WRITE_ZPD.
Controls in-shader emulation of the ZFail, StencilFail and Total ZPD counters to supplement both native and counter-based ZPass testing.
Enables VIZ_QUERY (VIZ) visibility tests for draws with a VIZ token. VIZ is the 360's version of conditional rendering / predication queries.

Read data written by memory export in shaders on the CPU. This may be needed in some games (but many only access exported data on the GPU, and this flag isn't needed to handle such behavior), but causes mid-frame synchronization, so it has a huge performance impact.
Controls CPU readback of render-to-texture resolve results.
Render target emulation path to use on Direct3D 12.
Render target emulation path to use on Vulkan.
Use approximate compare for alpha values to prevent flickering on NVIDIA graphics cards
Enable VSYNC.
Renders every tile of a predicated tiling frame at the same position as the depth prepass by applying the window offset in EDRAM rather than the viewport.
Rasterize 2x and 4x MSAA render targets at the Xenos sample positions, like real hardware, if the GPU and driver support it.
Post-processing anti-aliasing effect to apply to the image output of the game.
Dither the final image output from the internal precision to 8 bits per channel so gradients are smoother.
Additional sharpness for AMD FidelityFX Contrast Adaptive Sharpening (CAS), from 0 to 1.

xenia.l: Postprocess FFX FSR max upsampling passes
xenia.desc: Maximum number of upsampling passes performed in AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution 1.0 (FSR) before falling back to bilinear stretching after the final pass.
Sharpness reduction for AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution 1.0 (FSR), in stops.
Post-processing effect to use for resampling and/or sharpening of the final display output.
Maintain aspect ratio when stretching by displaying bars around the image when there's no more overscan area to crop out.
On graphics backends where this is supported, use the clear render pass load operation in presentation instead of clear commands clearing only the letterbox area.
Percentage of the image width that can be kept when presenting to maintain aspect ratio without letterboxing or stretching.
Percentage of the image height that can be kept when presenting to maintain aspect ratio without letterboxing or stretching.
Video modes
Custom width. See internal_display_resolution. Range 1-1920.
Custom height. See internal_display_resolution. Range 1-1080.
Enables usage of stereoscopic mode in titles.
Toggles interlaced mode.
Enables Music Player playback.
Decoder version used to process XMA audio.
Forward guide button presses to guest.
Defines deadzone level for left stick. Allowed range [0.0-1.0].
Defines deadzone level for right stick. Allowed range [0.0-1.0].
Toggle controller vibration.
Set license mask for activated content.
Apply title updates.
Ignores game-specified thread affinities.
Ignores game-specified thread priorities.
Display gamma to use with kernel_display_gamma_type 3.
Display gamma type: 0 - linear, 1 - sRGB (CRT), 2 - BT.709 (HDTV), 3 - power specified via kernel_display_gamma_power.
Allows to ignore 4k offset for physical allocations with provided range. Certain titles check if result matches provided lower range.
Verbose FFmpeg output (debug and above)
Enables XMA decoding on separate thread. Disabled should produce better results, but decrease performance a bit.
GPR compared to
comparison operator
truncate value to 32-bits
value compared against
int3 on JITed __debugbreak requests.
int3 before the given guest address is executed.
Break into the debugger on startup.
Break to the host debugger (or crash if no debugger attached) if an unimplemented PowerPC instruction is encountered.
Disable scaling code. Time management and locking is bypassed. Guest system time is directly pulled from host.
On x64, Use the RDTSC instruction as the time source. Requires invariant TSC. On a64, Use the CNTVCT_EL0 register as the time source
Log debugprint traps to the active debugger
Disables Context Promotion optimizations, this may be needed for some sports games, but will reduce performance.
Disables caching records of called instructions/mmio accesses.

Disables translating ppc prefetch/cache flush instructions to host prefetch/cacheflush instructions. This may improve performance as these instructions were written with the Xbox 360's cache in mind, and modern processors do their own automatic prefetching.
Disassemble functions during generation.
dumps translated hir
Eliminate e0 check on some memory accesses, like to r13(tls) or r1(sp)
Emit inline MMIO range checks for all I32 loads/stores instead of relying on exception-based MMIO detection.

xenia.l: Emit MMIO aware stores for recorded exception addresses
xenia.desc: Uses info gathered via record_mmio_access_exceptions to emit special stores that are faster than trapping the exception
Add extra movs and nops to make disassembly easier to read.
Enable pre-compiling guest functions that we know we've called/that we've recognized as being functions via simple heuristics, good for error finding/stress testing with the JIT
For developer use to analyze the quality of the generated code, not intended for actual debugging of the code
Don't exit when an undefined extern is called.
Directly read cached guest clock without calling the LoadClock method (it gets repeatedly updated by calls from other threads)
Inline constant MMIO loads and stores.
For testing whether a game may have races with a broken reserved load/store impl
Not for users, breaks games. Skip rounding double values to single precision and back
Allow float constant evaluation, may produce incorrect results and break games math
Known PVR's.
For guest addresses records whether we caught any mmio accesses for them. This info can then be used on a subsequent run to instruct the recompiler to emit checks
Don't strip dead context stores to aid in debugging.
Generate tracing for function instruction coverage statistics.
Generate tracing for function result data.
Generate tracing for function address references.
Generate tracing for function statistics.
Use less accurate dot-product exception handling that converts all infinite results to QNaN.
Perform validation checks on the HIR during compilation.
Enables a program to write to its own code segments in memory.
Break on Direct3D 12 validation errors.
Break on Direct3D 12 validation warnings.
Enable Direct3D 12 and DXGI debug layer.
Disassemble DXBC shaders after generation.

Disassemble DXBC shaders after conversion to DXIL, if DXIL shaders are supported by the OS, and DirectX Shader Compiler DLLs available at https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/releases are present.

Number of threads used for graphics pipeline creation. -1 to calculate automatically (75% of logical CPU cores), a positive number to specify the number of threads explicitly (up to the number of logical CPU cores), 0 to disable multithreaded pipeline creation.
Graphics (direct) command queue scheduling priority, 0 - normal, 1 - high, 2 - global realtime (requires administrator privileges, may impact system responsibility)

xenia.l: D3D12 submit on primary buffer end
xenia.desc: Submit the command list when a PM4 primary buffer ends if it's possible to submit immediately to try to reduce frame latency.
Display tessellated surfaces as wireframe for debugging.
Not useful to non-developers. Allows code to write to paths relative to game://. Used for generating test data to compare with original hardware.
Allow debugging and retain debug information.

xenia.l: Depth float24 convert in pixel shader
xenia.desc: Whether to convert the depth values to 24-bit floating-point (20e4) from the host precision (32-bit floating point) directly in the pixel shaders of guest draws when using a host depth buffer.

Whether to round to the nearest even, rather than truncating (rounding towards zero), the depth when converting it to 24-bit floating-point (20e4) from the host precision (32-bit floating point) when using a host depth buffer.

Use pixel shader stencil reference output where available for purposes like copying between render targets. Can be disabled for scalability testing, in this case, much more expensive drawing of 8 quads will be done.
Lower end of the fake sample count value written on EVENT_WRITE_ZPD when real occlusion queries are disabled.
Upper end of the fake sample count value written on EVENT_WRITE_ZPD when real occlusion queries are disabled.
When resolution scaling and readback resolve are enabled, resolve downscaling keeps one supersample out of each scaled pixel block.

xenia.l: Resolve resolution scale fill half pixel offset
xenia.desc: When using resolution scaling, apply the hack that stretches the first surely covered host pixel in the left and top sides of render target resolve areas to eliminate the gap caused by the half-pixel offset (this is necessary for certain games to display the scene graphics).
Disable RoundingModeRTE capability in SPIR-V shaders. Enable this to allow shader debugging in RenderDoc, which doesn't support this capability.
Dump textures to DDS

Matches interlock behavior by handling disjoint color and depth aliases for host render targets, keeping read-only depth bound when color writes only the unused stencil bits. May slightly increase overhead from keeping both host targets live and bound.

Use 4x MSAA with 2 samples instead of native 2x MSAA when available. For scalability testing on host GPU APIs where 2x is not mandatory. MSAA will be of a similar or worse quality and use more memory.

When transferring data between depth render targets, use the "not equal" test to avoid writing rewriting depth via shader depth output if it's the same as the one currently in the depth buffer in case of round trips of the data.
Disassemble Xenos instructions as comments in the resulting DXBC for debugging.

Use switch rather than if for flow control. Turning this off or on may improve stability, though this heavily depends on the driver - on AMD, it's recommended to have this set to true, as some titles appear to crash when if is used for flow control (possibly the shader compiler tries to flatten them). On Intel HD Graphics, this is ignored because of a crash with the switch instruction.

xenia.l: Execute unclipped draw vs on CPU
xenia.desc: Execute the vertex shader for draws with clipping disabled, primarily screen-space draws (such as clears), on the CPU when possible to estimate the extent of the EDRAM involved in the draw.

xenia.l: Execute unclipped draw vs on CPU for psi render backend
xenia.desc: If execute_unclipped_draw_vs_on_cpu is enabled, execute the vertex shader for unclipped draws on the CPU even when using the pixel shader interlock (rasterizer-ordered view) implementation of the render backend on the host, for which no expensive copying between host render targets is needed when the ownership of a EDRAM range is changed.

xenia.l: Execute unclipped draw vs on CPU with scissor
xenia.desc: Don't restrict the usage of execute_unclipped_draw_vs_on_cpu to only non-scissored draws (with the right and the bottom sides of the scissor rectangle at 8192 or beyond) even though if the scissor rectangle is present, it's usually sufficient for esimating the height of the render target.

xenia.l: Force convert line loops to strips
xenia.desc: For host graphics API downlevel support testing only, force CPU conversion of line loops to line strips even if the host supports line loop primitives natively.

xenia.l: Force convert quad lists to triangle lists
xenia.desc: For host graphics API downlevel support testing only, force CPU conversion of quad lists to quad strips even if the host supports quad list primitives natively or via geometry shader emulation.

xenia.l: Force convert triangle fans to lists
xenia.desc: For host graphics API downlevel support testing only, force CPU conversion of triangle fans to triangle lists even if the host supports triangle fan primitives natively.

When the host can't write 8 bits per component pixels with piecewise linear gamma encoding directly with correct blending, use the 16-bit unsigned normalized format, if supported, for conceptually correct 8_8_8_8_GAMMA render target format blending in linear color space. Greatly increases accuracy for this format, but may result in render target copying costs if the game switches between 8_8_8_8_GAMMA and 8_8_8_8 views for the same EDRAM render target.

Enable support of vertex half-pixel offset (D3D9 PA_SU_VTX_CNTL PIX_CENTER). Generally games are aware of the half-pixel offset, and having this enabled is the correct behavior (disabling this may significantly break post-processing in some games), but in certain games it might have been ignored, resulting in slight blurriness of UI textures, for instance, when they are read between texels rather than at texel centers, or the leftmost/topmost pixels may not be fully covered when MSAA is used with fullscreen passes.

For host graphics API downlevel testing only (useful only for Qualcomm Adreno 4xx-level host GPU testing), force indirection or pre-masking and pre-swapping of 32-bit vertex indices as if the host only supports 24-bit indices.

xenia.l: Mrt EDRAM used range clamp to min
xenia.desc: With host render targets, if multiple render targets are bound, estimate the EDRAM range modified in any of them to be not bigger than the distance between any two render targets in the EDRAM, rather than allowing the last one claim the rest of the EDRAM.

xenia.l: Native stencil value output d3d12 intel
xenia.desc: Allow stencil reference output usage on Direct3D 12 on Intel GPUs - not working on UHD Graphics 630 as of March 2021 (driver 27.20.0100.8336).

xenia.l: No discard stencil in transfer pipelines
xenia.desc: Skip stencil bit discard in render target transfer pipelines. May improve performance on some GPUs.
Disable filtering between cube map faces near edges where possible (Vulkan with VK_EXT_non_seamless_cube_map) to reproduce the Direct3D 9 behavior.
Smallest number of guest indices to store in the cache to try reusing later in the same frame if processing (such as primitive type conversion or reset index replacement) is performed.

When the host can only support 16_16 and 16_16_16_16 render targets as -1...1, remap -32...32 to -1...1 to use the full possible range of values, at the expense of multiplicative blending correctness.
Store shaders persistently and load them when loading games to avoid runtime spikes and freezes when playing the game not for the first time.
Maximum host texture memory usage (in megabytes) above which textures will be destroyed as soon as possible.

xenia.l: Texture cache memory limit render to texture
xenia.desc: Part of the host texture memory budget (in megabytes) that will be scaled by the current drawing resolution scale.
Maximum host texture memory usage (in megabytes) above which old textures will be destroyed.

xenia.l: Texture cache memory limit soft lifetime
xenia.desc: Seconds a texture should be unused to be considered old enough to be deleted if texture memory usage exceeds texture_cache_memory_limit_soft.

xenia.l: Vulkan allow present mode fifo relaxed
xenia.desc: When available, allow the relaxed first-in-first-out presentation mode (3rd priority), which causes waiting for host display vertical sync, but may present with tearing if frames don't meet the host display refresh rate.

When available, allow the immediate presentation mode (1st priority), offering the lowest latency with the possibility of tearing in certain cases, and, depending on the configuration, variable refresh rate.
When available, allow the mailbox presentation mode (2nd priority), offering low latency without the possibility of tearing.
Write Vulkan VK_EXT_debug_utils messages to the Xenia log, as opposed to the OS debug output.

Number of threads used for graphics pipeline creation. -1 to calculate automatically (75% of logical CPU cores), a positive number to specify the number of threads explicitly (up to the number of logical CPU cores), 0 to disable multithreaded pipeline creation.
Wait for presentation queue idle before each frame to prevent semaphore reuse. May fix rendering issues but causes significant performance loss.
Enable sparse binding for shared memory emulation. Disabling it increases video memory usage - a 512 MB buffer is created - but allows graphics debuggers that don't support sparse binding to work.
Enable the Vulkan validation layer (VK_LAYER_KHRONOS_validation). Messages will be written to the Xenia log if 'vulkan_log_debug_messages' is enabled, or to the OS debug output otherwise.
Aligns the start of all basic blocks to N bytes. Only specify a power of 2, 16 is the recommended value. Results in larger icache usage, but potentially faster loops
implement the db16cyc instruction via MaybeYield, may improve scheduling of guest threads
Records entries for guest/host stack mappings at function starts and checks for reentry at return sites. Has slight performance impact, but fixes crashes in games that use setjmp/longjmp.
